sources.entry: 🧰 codingknite/frontend-development: a list of resources for frontend development

summary.one_liner: A curated, link-only list of learning resources, tools, and career material for frontend web development, organized by topic.
summary.what_it_does: This is an "awesome"-style list rather than software: it collects links to frontend learning material and is explicitly described as a reference, not a guide. It is organized into sections such as How the Internet Works, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Git, React, Vue, icons, fonts, illustrations, color palettes, stock images, hosting providers, design and portfolio inspiration, YouTube channels, podcasts, blogs, interview prep, and newsletters. Each entry is tagged by type (documentation, courses, books, websites, videos, podcasts) and paid resources are marked with a 💵 symbol. Most entries are one-line links with brief descriptions, and many sections end with a back-to-top link. The README also includes a contributor list and a note inviting contributions.
use_cases: Finding free or paid courses to learn HTML, CSS, or JavaScript
Picking a React or Vue learning path and related tools
Looking up CSS frameworks, icon sets, or color palettes for a web project
Finding stock images, fonts, or illustrations for a website
Preparing for frontend job interviews and finding remote job boards
Finding frontend YouTube channels, podcasts, and newsletters to follow
notable: Sections are organized by frontend topic, with Vue and React given their own detailed breakdowns
Paid resources are flagged with a 💵 marker so free and paid options are easy to tell apart
Covers non-code material too: design inspiration, stock media, color tools, resume templates, and job sites
Includes a 'Challenge Websites' section listing coding practice platforms and a 'Practice your CSS Skills' section of online editors
caveats: Link-only list with no code; entries are not verified or dated in the README and some may be out of date
Mixes free and paid resources, and the README does not say which entries require payment beyond the 💵 marker
The README states it is a reference rather than a guided learning path
